memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Like a lion they crouch and lie down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse them? May those who bless you be blessed and those who curse you be cursed!" - Num 24:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The third oracle closes with an echo of God's ancient promise to Abraham: those who bless Israel will be blessed, and those who curse them will be cursed. Balaam, hired to curse, ends up pronouncing blessing and warning that anyone who curses God's people invites a curse upon themselves.

This takes us back to the covenant God made with Abraham long before. God had bound Himself to protect and prosper the line of promise, and here that promise stands firm even on the lips of a foreign prophet. God's word to Abraham had not failed; it was being confirmed in the plains of Moab.

The image of the lion at rest is powerful. Israel could lie down securely, undisturbed, because God guarded them. Who would dare rouse a lion? Their safety came not from constant vigilance but from the God who watched over them. They could rest because He was awake.

This promise to Abraham finds its ultimate fulfilment in Christ, through whom all nations are blessed (Gal 3:8). We do not claim national protection as Israel did, but we rest in the same faithful God who guards His people in Christ. In Him we can lie down in peace, for the Lord watches over us and no one can finally snatch us from His hand (John 10:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rest secure in God's protection, or live in constant anxiety?
2. How does God's faithfulness to Abraham encourage your trust today?
3. What does it mean to "lie down" in the peace God gives in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that I can rest secure under Your watchful care. Help me to lie down in peace, trusting that in Christ no one can snatch me from Your hand. Amen.
